### equity data

```{r}
## Use the official-code vulnerability layer retained by the revised health
## workflow. This avoids the historical row-order join used by the exploratory
## notebook and makes every health-vulnerability match auditable by LSOA11CD.
f <- './data/derived/fig7_vulnerability_lsoa11_fig7_revised_equal_area.gpkg'

# --- metrics ---
metrics <- c(
  "pIncomeDeprivation",
  "p5under",
  "p75over",
  "pNotEnglishProficient", # removed later
  "pSocial_housing",       # removed later
  "pBAME",
  "SVI"                    # "overall_score"
)


metrics_full <- metrics

# short names
metrics_full_short <- c(
  'Income deprivation',
  "Age <5", 
  "Age ≥75",
  "Limited English",
  "Social housing",
  "Ethnic minority",
  "SVI"
)


svi_lsoa <- st_read(f, quiet = TRUE) %>%
  rename('SVI' = 'overall_score') %>%
  # ----- pooled quintiles for all EP_* variables -----
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(metrics),
      ~ {
        brks <- quantile(.x, probs = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2), na.rm = TRUE, type = 7)
        brks <- unique(brks)                       # handle duplicate quantiles
        if (length(brks) < 2) {
          # all values identical or mostly NA: return all-NA factor with Q1–Q5 levels
          factor(NA_real_, levels = paste0("Q", 1:5))
        } else {
          labs <- paste0("Q", seq_len(length(brks) - 1))
          cut(.x, breaks = brks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = labs)
        }
      },
      .names = "{.col}_q"
    )
  )

names(svi_lsoa)



svi_lsoa_subset <- svi_lsoa %>%
  ## remove percentile cols 
  dplyr::select(-ends_with('_pct'))


# 2. Calculate quintiles and add them as a new column -- the same result as above
# We use ntile() from dplyr for easy splitting, or cut() with quantile() for base R
df <- svi_lsoa %>%
  mutate(quintile = factor(ntile(pIncomeDeprivation, 5)))
```

```{r}
  # Select only the columns you want + pivot them to long format
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(metrics), 
               names_to = "Metric",

  group_by(Metric) %>%
```

### health data

The LSOA inputs were generated by `health-modeling-zonal-stats.ipynb`.
All health analyses intentionally hold population and baseline mortality at
2021 values while applying the 2050 temperature fields. Results therefore
isolate the climate and land-cover scenarios and should not be described as a
projection of London's 2050 population.

```{r}
health_file <- './data/derived/health_lsoa_fig7_revised_equal_area_population_weighted_2021.csv'
population_file <- './data/derived/lsoa_population_2021_by_lsoa11cd.csv'

stopifnot(file.exists(health_file), file.exists(population_file))

population_2021 <- read_csv(population_file, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  select(LSOA11CD, population_2021)
if (anyDuplicated(population_2021$LSOA11CD)) {
  stop("The 2021 LSOA population table contains duplicate LSOA11CD values.")
}

# Figure 6 uses the primary 25 C setting. The 28 C results remain a documented
# sensitivity analysis and should not be pooled with the primary model.
health_df <- read_csv(health_file, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(temperature_setting_c == 25) %>%
  transmute(
    LSOA11CD,
    Neighborhood_name,
    cases_abs = deaths_averted,
    lc_scenario = factor(lc_scenario, levels = c("Green30", "Target30")),
    indicator,
    cases_meaning = "Deaths averted per 100,000 residents"
  )

if (anyDuplicated(health_df[c("LSOA11CD", "lc_scenario", "indicator")])) {
  stop("The revised health table contains duplicate LSOA/scenario/cause rows.")
}


unique(health_df$lc_scenario)
```



### join data

```{r}
## Join only by the official statistical-area code. Population normalization
## prevents large LSOAs from appearing to receive larger benefits merely
## because they contain more residents.
health_sf <- svi_lsoa_subset %>%
  left_join(health_df, by = 'LSOA11CD') %>%
  left_join(population_2021, by = 'LSOA11CD') %>%
  mutate(cases = 100000 * cases_abs / population_2021)

if (anyNA(health_sf$cases) || any(!is.finite(health_sf$cases))) {
  stop("The health, vulnerability or population join is incomplete.")
}


label_map <- c(
  p75over        = "Age ≥75",

  pIncomeDeprivation = "Income deprivation",
  p5under        = "Age <5"
)
```

How to select the "Best" representative?

```{r collinearity }

# Check correlation among your metrics
library(ggcorrplot)

# 1. Select only the numeric metric columns
# We also include 'cases' to see which metrics correlate most strongly with the outcome

## 1.1. include `cases` in the plot ---
corr_vars <- 
  # df_scaled %>%
  df_cont_copy %>% 
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(all_of(metrics_full), cases)
corr_fix <- ''


## 1.2. NOT include `cases` in the plot ---
corr_vars <-
  df_cont_copy %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(all_of(metrics_full))
names(corr_vars) <- metrics_full_short
corr_fix <- 'short'



# 2. Compute the correlation matrix --------------------------------------------
# use = "complete.obs" handles missing values by ignoring rows with NAs
cor_matrix <- cor(corr_vars, use = "complete.obs", method = "pearson")

# 3. Compute P-values and FORCE TO MATRIX
p_mat <- ggcorrplot::cor_pmat(corr_vars)
p_mat <- as.matrix(p_mat)  # <--- This fixes the "Subscript" error

# 4. Plot
ggcorrplot(cor_matrix,
           method = "square",
           type = "lower",
           lab = TRUE,
           lab_size = 3,
           p.mat = p_mat,          # Now passing a safe matrix
           sig.level = 0.05,
           insig = "blank",
           colors = c("#d73027", "white", "#2c7bb6"),
           # title = "Correlation Matrix", 
           ggtheme = theme_minimal(base_size = 10)) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank()
  )

f <- paste0('./figures/', paste0('health_outcome_equity_cor_', corr_fix, '.png'))
ggsave(plot = last_plot(), filename = f, width = 7, height = 5, units = 'in', dpi = 300)
```

### boxplot

```{r data}

# Calculate the typical range (e.g., 5th to 95th percentile) to determine zoom limits automatically
lower_bound_cat <- quantile(df_cat2$cases, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
upper_bound_cat <- quantile(df_cat2$cases, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)
  
# 1. Define a function to calculate N and position it
stat_box_data <- function(y) {
  return( 
    data.frame(
      y = max(y, na.rm = T) * 1.05,  # Position: Just above the max value (whisker or outlier)
      label = paste0("n = ", length(y)) # Label: "n = 123"
    )
  )
}

stat_box_data_bottom <- function(y) {
  return( 
    data.frame(
      y = min(y, na.rm = T) - (max(y, na.rm = T) - min(y, na.rm = T)) * 0.05, # Just below min
      label = length(y) # simple number "123" (cleaner for bottom axis)
    )
  )
}
```

```{r brackets, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}

library(ggpubr)  # For plotting p-values
library(rstatix) # For calculating the tests easily

# 1. Run the Pairwise Wilcoxon Test
# We group by 'Metric' so the test is done separately for each panel
stat_test <- df_cat2 %>%
  group_by(Metric) %>%
  wilcox_test(cases ~ Quintile) %>%
  adjust_pvalue(method = "bonferroni") %>% # Adjust for multiple comparisons to avoid false positives
  add_significance() %>%                   # Adds stars (*, **, ns)
  filter(p.adj < 0.05) %>%                 # <--- THIS LINE removes non-significant pairs
  add_xy_position(x = "Quintile", fun = 'median_iqr', step.increase = 1) # Auto-calculates bracket height

# 2. Plot
ggplot(df_cat2, aes(x = Quintile, y = cases, fill = Quintile)) +
  
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  
  # Add the p-values manually using the dataframe we created above
  stat_pvalue_manual(
    stat_test, 
    color = 'gray',
    label = "p.adj.signif", # Use stars (*, **) instead of numbers
    tip.length = 0.01,      # Length of the bracket tips
    hide.ns = TRUE          # Double check to ensure NS are hidden
  ) +
  
  facet_wrap(~Metric, scales = "free_y") +
  
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(lower_bound_cat, upper_bound_cat)) + # Zooms the view without deleting data
  # Important: Add extra space at the top for the brackets
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.5))) +
  
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Spectral", direction = -1) +
  labs(title = "Significant Pairwise Differences by Quintile",
       subtitle = "Only significant comparisons (p.adj < 0.05) are shown",
       y = "Cases") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

  To use the Compact Letter Display (CLD) method (where *groups sharing the same letter are not significantly different*), you need to combine a statistical test with the multcompView package.
  Since you are likely using non-parametric data (given the previous discussion on Quintiles/Cases), here is the robust workflow using *Dunn’s Test* (the post-hoc test for Kruskal-Wallis) to generate the letters.
  
```{r cld}

library(multcompView)
library(rstatix)


# 1. Define a helper function to generate letters for one metric
get_cld_letters <- function(data) {
  # Run Dunn's Test (Non-parametric pairwise)
  dunn_res <- dunn_test(data, cases ~ Quintile, p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")
  
  # Format p-values for multcompView ("Group1-Group2" = p.val)
  p_values <- setNames(dunn_res$p.adj, paste(dunn_res$group1, dunn_res$group2, sep = "-"))
  
  # Convert p-values to Letters
  letters_list <- multcompLetters(p_values)$Letters
  
  # Return as a dataframe
  return(data.frame(Quintile = names(letters_list), Letter = letters_list))
}

# 2. Apply this function to every Metric group
cld_data <- df_cat2 %>%
  group_by(Metric) %>%
  # Nest data to run the function per group
  nest() %>%
  mutate(cld = purrr::map(data, get_cld_letters)) %>%
  unnest(cld) %>%
  select(Metric, Quintile, Letter)

# 3. Calculate Y-positions (Just above the highest outlier per group)
# This ensures the letter sits nicely on top of the boxplot
y_positions <- df_cat2 %>%
  group_by(Metric, Quintile) %>%
  summarise(
    # max_y = max(cases, na.rm = TRUE), 
    max_y = quantile(cases, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE),  # 95th percentile
    q3  = quantile(cases, 0.75 + 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), # add a bit more for better viz
    iqr = IQR(cases, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Add a little buffer (5% of height) so the letter doesn't touch the whisker
  mutate(
    upper_cap = q3 + 1.5 * iqr,
    max_y     = q3,
    y_pos = max_y * 1.05) 

# 4. Merge Letters with Positions
final_labels <- left_join(cld_data, y_positions, by = c("Metric", "Quintile"))

# Check the result
head(final_labels)



## Step 3: Plot with Letters
ggplot(df_cat2, aes(x = Quintile, y = cases, fill = Quintile)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  # geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = 1, outlier.size = 1, outlier.alpha = 0.2) + # Show outliers lightly
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + 
  
  # Add the Letters
  geom_text(data = final_labels, 
            aes(x = Quintile, y = y_pos, label = Letter), 
            vjust = 0, # Sits right on the y_pos line
            color = 'gray50',hjust = -0.2,
            size = 3, 
            fontface = "bold") +
  
  facet_wrap(~Metric, 
             labeller = labeller(Metric = label_map),
             scales = "free_y") +
  
  # Expand Y axis slightly to fit the letters
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.1, 0.2))) +
  
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(lower_bound_cat, upper_bound_cat)) + # Zooms the view without deleting data
  
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Spectral", direction = -1) +
  labs(title = paste0("Differences by Quintile (", lc_snr, ")"),
       caption = "Groups sharing the same letter are not significantly different (Dunn's Test, p < 0.05)",
       y = str_to_sentence(cases_meaning_lab)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

f <- paste0('./figures/', paste('equity_health', outcome_ind, 'q_cld', lc_snr, ymd, sep = '_'), '.png'); f
ggsave(plot = last_plot(), filename = f, width = 7, height = 5, units = 'in', dpi = 300)
```

```{r lm - coef}

library(broom)
library(purrr)


# 1. Standardize predictors (Z-score) so coefficients are comparable
# df_scaled

# 2. Run regressions and create significance columns
models <- map_dfr(metrics, function(m) {
  formula <- as.formula(paste("cases ~", m))
  broom::tidy(lm(formula, data = df_scaled), conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    mutate(Metric = m)
}) %>%
  # Create significance categories and stars
  mutate(
    # Create a categorical column for coloring
    Significance = ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "Significant", "Not Significant"),
    
    # Create a text column for stars
    Stars = case_when(
      p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE            ~ ""
    )
  )

# 3. Plot the coefficients (Forest Plot)
# 3. Plot with Significance highlighting
ggplot(models, aes(x = estimate, y = reorder(Metric, estimate), color = Significance)) +
  # Add vertical line at 0 (Null effect)
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  
  # Error bars
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = 0.2) +
  
  # The Point Estimate
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  
  # Add the Stars just slightly above the point
  geom_text(aes(label = Stars), vjust = -0.8, show.legend = FALSE, size = 5) +
  
  # Manual colors: Blue for significant, Gray for not
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Significant" = "#2c7bb6", "Not Significant" = "gray70")) +
  
  labs(title = paste("Standardized Effect Sizes on", outcome_ind, "Cases", sep = " "), 
       caption = "Statistically significant associations are highlighted in blue (* p<0.05)",
       x = "Coefficient Estimate (Change in Cases per 1 SD)",
       y = "") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.8, 0.1))

f <- paste0('./figures/', paste('equity_health', outcome_ind, 'coef', lc_snr, ymd, sep = '_'), '.png'); f
# ggsave(plot = last_plot(), filename = f, width = 7, height = 5, units = 'in', dpi = 300)
```

Fig. x | Standardized associations between social vulnerability indicators and preventable cases. Estimates represent the change in preventable case rate per one standard deviation (SD) increase in each vulnerability metric (linear regression coefficients). Error bars denote 95% confidence intervals. Points colored in blue indicate statistically significant associations (P<0.05); gray points indicate non-significance. All metrics are standardized (Z-scores) to allow for direct comparison of effect sizes.



  
### Production Figure 6 GAM analysis

The models retain the original per-100,000 fitting scale; Figure 6 and its
contrast tables report deaths averted per million residents. We use all valid
LSOAs and the documented 25 °C Green30 run. The 1st–99th percentile analysis is
retained only as a sensitivity check because metric-specific trimming otherwise
changes the sample from panel to panel. Reported intervals are conditional on
the fitted GAM and do not propagate uncertainty from UCM temperatures,
population, mortality inputs or exposure–response coefficients.

```{r figure-6-production-models}
library(mgcv)

figure6_metrics <- c(
  "pIncomeDeprivation", "p5under", "p75over", "pBAME", "SVI"
)
figure6_labels <- c(
  pIncomeDeprivation = "Income deprivation",
  p5under = "Age <5",
  p75over = "Age ≥75",
  pBAME = "Ethnic-minority population share",
  SVI = "Social Vulnerability Index"
)
figure6_scenario <- "Green30"
figure6_outcome <- "All_cause"
figure6_k <- 10L
figure6_moran_permutations <- 999L
figure6_seed <- 20260908L
figure6_output_dir <- here("figures", "figure6_statistical_reporting")
dir.create(figure6_output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

figure6_sf <- health_sf %>%
  filter(indicator == figure6_outcome, lc_scenario == figure6_scenario) %>%
  select(LSOA11CD, cases, all_of(figure6_metrics)) %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(cases),
    if_all(all_of(figure6_metrics), ~ is.finite(.x))
  ) %>%
  arrange(LSOA11CD) %>%
  mutate(row_id = row_number())

if (nrow(figure6_sf) < 100 || anyDuplicated(figure6_sf$LSOA11CD)) {
  stop("Figure 6 requires one valid Green30 all-cause record per LSOA.")
}

# Standardizing predictors makes curves comparable without changing model fit.
figure6_sf <- figure6_sf %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(figure6_metrics), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x))))

# Queen-contiguity neighbours support a dependency-free residual Moran's I
# check. This is a diagnostic sensitivity test, not a replacement spatial model.
figure6_neighbours <- sf::st_touches(figure6_sf)
edge_i <- rep(seq_along(figure6_neighbours), lengths(figure6_neighbours))
edge_j <- unlist(figure6_neighbours, use.names = FALSE)
keep_edge <- edge_i < edge_j
figure6_edges <- tibble(i = edge_i[keep_edge], j = edge_j[keep_edge])
if (nrow(figure6_edges) == 0) stop("No LSOA neighbour links were identified.")

moran_permutation <- function(values, edges, permutations, seed) {
  x <- values - mean(values)
  n <- length(x)
  expected <- -1 / (n - 1)
  denominator <- sum(x^2)
  observed <- (n / (2 * nrow(edges))) *
    (2 * sum(x[edges$i] * x[edges$j])) / denominator

  set.seed(seed)
  simulated <- replicate(permutations, {
    xp <- sample(x, replace = FALSE)
    (n / (2 * nrow(edges))) *
      (2 * sum(xp[edges$i] * xp[edges$j])) / denominator
  })
  tibble(
    moran_i = observed,
    expected_i = expected,
    permutation_p_two_sided =
      (1 + sum(abs(simulated - expected) >= abs(observed - expected))) /
      (permutations + 1),
    permutations = permutations,
    neighbour_links = nrow(edges)
  )
}

fit_figure6_gam <- function(data, metric, analysis_label, calculate_spatial = FALSE) {
  model_data <- data %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    transmute(row_id, cases, x = .data[[metric]])

  # A robust scaled-t family reduces sensitivity to genuine extreme mortality
  # benefits while retaining all observations in the primary model.
  model <- mgcv::gam(
    cases ~ s(x, k = figure6_k, bs = "ts"),
    data = model_data,
    family = mgcv::scat(), method = "REML", select = TRUE
  )

  # Compare functional form in a Gaussian-ML sensitivity analysis. The scaled-t
  # linear ML fit is numerically unstable in mgcv, while REML AIC values from
  # models with different fixed-effect structures are not comparable.
  smooth_ml <- mgcv::gam(
    cases ~ s(x, k = figure6_k, bs = "ts"), data = model_data,
    family = gaussian(), method = "ML", select = TRUE
  )
  linear_ml <- mgcv::gam(
    cases ~ x, data = model_data,
    family = gaussian(), method = "ML"
  )

  model_summary <- summary(model)
  smooth_table <- model_summary$s.table
  stat_column <- intersect(c("F", "Chi.sq"), colnames(smooth_table))
  # k.check uses random subsampling/permutations: seed it independently of Moran's I.
  set.seed(figure6_seed)
  k_table <- mgcv::k.check(model)

  x_quantiles <- quantile(model_data$x, c(0.10, 0.90), na.rm = TRUE)
  contrast_data <- data.frame(x = unname(x_quantiles))
  contrast_matrix <- predict(model, newdata = contrast_data, type = "lpmatrix")
  contrast_vector <- contrast_matrix[2, ] - contrast_matrix[1, ]
  contrast_estimate <- drop(contrast_vector %*% coef(model))
  contrast_se <- sqrt(drop(
    contrast_vector %*% vcov(model) %*% contrast_vector
  ))

  prediction_data <- data.frame(
    x = seq(min(model_data$x), max(model_data$x), length.out = 200)
  )
  term_prediction <- predict(
    model, newdata = prediction_data, type = "terms", se.fit = TRUE
  )

  stats <- tibble(
    Analysis = analysis_label,
    Metric = metric,
    N = nrow(model_data),
    EDF = unname(smooth_table[1, "edf"]),
    Ref_df = if ("Ref.df" %in% colnames(smooth_table)) {
      unname(smooth_table[1, "Ref.df"])
    } else NA_real_,
    Test_Type = if (length(stat_column)) stat_column[[1]] else NA_character_,
    Test_Statistic = if (length(stat_column)) {
      unname(smooth_table[1, stat_column[[1]]])
    } else NA_real_,
    P_Value = unname(smooth_table[1, "p-value"]),
    Adj_R_Sq = unname(model_summary$r.sq),
    Deviance_Explained = unname(model_summary$dev.expl),
    AIC_GAM_ML = AIC(smooth_ml),
    AIC_Linear_ML = AIC(linear_ml),
    Delta_AIC_Linear_minus_GAM = AIC(linear_ml) - AIC(smooth_ml),
    Basis_k = figure6_k,
    K_Index = unname(k_table[1, "k-index"]),
    K_Check_P = unname(k_table[1, "p-value"]),
    Family = model$family$family,
    Method = "REML",
    AIC_Comparison = "Gaussian ML sensitivity: linear minus smooth"
  )

  contrast <- tibble(
    Analysis = analysis_label,
    Metric = metric,
    Predictor_P10 = x_quantiles[[1]],
    Predictor_P90 = x_quantiles[[2]],
    Difference_P90_minus_P10 = contrast_estimate,
    Difference_SE = contrast_se,
    Difference_CI_Low = contrast_estimate - 1.96 * contrast_se,
    Difference_CI_High = contrast_estimate + 1.96 * contrast_se
  )

  curve <- tibble(
    Analysis = analysis_label,
    Metric = metric,
    x = prediction_data$x,
    y = drop(term_prediction$fit),
    se = drop(term_prediction$se.fit)
  )

  spatial <- if (calculate_spatial) {
    moran_permutation(
      residuals(model, type = "deviance"), figure6_edges,
      figure6_moran_permutations,
      figure6_seed + match(metric, figure6_metrics)
    ) %>% mutate(Analysis = analysis_label, Metric = metric, .before = 1)
  } else {
    tibble()
  }

  list(stats = stats, contrast = contrast, curve = curve, spatial = spatial)
}

primary_results <- purrr::map(figure6_metrics, function(metric) {
  fit_figure6_gam(figure6_sf, metric, "Primary: all valid LSOAs", TRUE)
})

# The sensitivity analysis reproduces the earlier trimming choice while making
# its reduced, metric-specific sample size explicit.
trimmed_results <- purrr::map(figure6_metrics, function(metric) {
  limits <- quantile(figure6_sf[[metric]], c(0.01, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE)
  trimmed <- figure6_sf %>%
    filter(.data[[metric]] >= limits[[1]], .data[[metric]] <= limits[[2]])
  fit_figure6_gam(trimmed, metric, "Sensitivity: predictor P1-P99", FALSE)
})

all_results <- c(primary_results, trimmed_results)
model_stats_table <- bind_rows(purrr::map(all_results, "stats")) %>%
  group_by(Analysis) %>%
  mutate(P_Value_BH = p.adjust(P_Value, method = "BH")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    Metric_Label = recode(Metric, !!!figure6_labels),
    P_Value_Display = format.pval(P_Value, digits = 3, eps = 0.001),
    P_Value_BH_Display = format.pval(P_Value_BH, digits = 3, eps = 0.001),
    Signif_Code = case_when(
      P_Value_BH < 0.001 ~ "***",
      P_Value_BH < 0.01 ~ "**",
      P_Value_BH < 0.05 ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ "ns"
    )
  )

figure6_contrasts <- bind_rows(purrr::map(all_results, "contrast")) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("Difference_"), ~ 10 * .x), rate_denominator = 1000000L) %>%
  mutate(Metric_Label = recode(Metric, !!!figure6_labels))
df_cont_curve <- bind_rows(purrr::map(primary_results, "curve")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(y, se), ~ 10 * .x), rate_denominator = 1000000L) %>%
  mutate(Metric_Label = recode(Metric, !!!figure6_labels))
figure6_spatial_diagnostics <- bind_rows(purrr::map(primary_results, "spatial")) %>%
  mutate(Metric_Label = recode(Metric, !!!figure6_labels))

# Large, significant residual Moran's I means the conventional GAM P values
# should be treated as descriptive until a spatial model is agreed and reported.
figure6_spatial_flag <- any(
  figure6_spatial_diagnostics$permutation_p_two_sided < 0.05 &
    abs(figure6_spatial_diagnostics$moran_i) > 0.10
)
df_cont_raw <- figure6_sf %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(all_of(figure6_metrics)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "x") %>%
  mutate(Metric_Label = recode(Metric, !!!figure6_labels))

readr::write_csv(model_stats_table, file.path(
  figure6_output_dir, "figure6_gam_model_reporting.csv"
))
readr::write_csv(figure6_contrasts, file.path(
  figure6_output_dir, "figure6_gam_p10_p90_contrasts.csv"
))
readr::write_csv(df_cont_curve, file.path(
  figure6_output_dir, "figure6_gam_curve_data.csv"
))
readr::write_csv(figure6_spatial_diagnostics, file.path(
  figure6_output_dir, "figure6_gam_residual_morans_i.csv"
))
readr::write_csv(tibble(
  file = c(health_file, population_file,
           './data/derived/fig7_vulnerability_lsoa11_fig7_revised_equal_area.gpkg'),
  md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(file))
), file.path(figure6_output_dir, "figure6_input_checksums.csv"))
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), file.path(
  figure6_output_dir, "figure6_session_info.txt"
))
writeLines(
  if (figure6_spatial_flag) {
    paste(
      "Interpretation gate: strong residual spatial autocorrelation remains",
      "in every unadjusted GAM. Treat curves as descriptive and do not use",
      "their conventional P values as final inferential evidence until a",
      "pre-specified spatial model or spatial resampling analysis is completed."
    )
  } else {
    "No strong residual spatial autocorrelation was detected by the specified diagnostic."
  },
  file.path(figure6_output_dir, "figure6_interpretation_note.txt")
)
```

```{r - input data, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Loop through each metric
for (m in metrics) {
  
  cat("\n--- Processing metric:", m, "---\n")
  
  # --- A. CALCULATE PERCENTILES ---
  # Extract the column as a clean vector to safely calculate quantiles
  current_metric_data <- df_scaled[[m]]
  
  lower_bound <- quantile(current_metric_data, 0.01, na.rm = TRUE)
  upper_bound <- quantile(current_metric_data, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  cat("Lower bound (1%):", lower_bound, "\n")
  cat("Upper bound (99%):", upper_bound, "\n")
  
  # --- B. DYNAMIC TRIMMING ---
  # Create a temporary dataset specifically for this metric's model,
  # trimming the extreme top 1% and bottom 1% of outliers.
  df_scaled_i <- df_scaled %>%
    select(cases, all_of(m)) %>%  # Use all_of() for clarity
    filter(.data[[m]] >= lower_bound & .data[[m]] <= upper_bound) %>%
    rename(x_raw = all_of(m)) %>%  # Rename to x_raw
    mutate(Metric = m) %>%  # Add metric name
    select(cases, Metric, x_raw)  # Reorder columns
  
  cat("Rows retained:", nrow(df_scaled_i), "out of", nrow(df_scaled), "\n")
  
  # Append to main dataset
  df_scaled_robust <- rbind(df_scaled_robust, df_scaled_i)

  
}
```

```{r - gam data, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}

# 1. Standardize your data (optional, but helps compare "strength" visually)
# df_scaled_robust

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Prepare Raw Data for the Rug Plot
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# We need the raw data in long format so geom_rug knows 
# where the data points are for EACH metric.
# df_cont_raw <- df_scaled_robust %>%
#   select(all_of(metrics)) %>%
#   pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "x_raw")

df_cont_raw <- df_scaled_robust %>%
  select(-cases) 

k_i <- 10


# 2. Extract curve data for every metric
plot_data_list <- list()

# Initialize an empty list to store the stats
stats_list <- list()

for (m in metrics) {
  
  df_scaled_robust_i <- df_scaled_robust %>%
    dplyr::filter(Metric == m)
  
  m_i <- 'x_raw'
  
  # 1. DEFINE THE ROBUST GAM FORMULA
  # k = 5: Restricts wiggles to prevent overfitting noise.
  # bs = 'ts': Applies a thin-plate shrinkage penalty (forces curve to flat line if unsupported by data).
  # 1. Fit using the robust heavy-tailed distribution (scat)
  # 2. Keep k=10 to raise the ceiling, and bs='ts' for shrinkage
  formula <- as.formula(paste("cases ~ s(", m_i, ", k = ", k_i, ", bs = 'ts')"))
  # Option B (Adding double-penalty selection to the whole model - Highly Recommended)
  gam_model <- gam(formula, 
                   data = df_scaled_robust_i, 
                   method = "REML", 
                   # family = tw(),
                   family = scat(), # Universal robust family
                   select = TRUE)   # Dynamic shrinkage adapts to each scenario
  
  
  #####################################
  ## collect stats data for later use 
  #####################################
  # 2. Fit the Linear Model (The Baseline Comparison)
  formula_lm <- as.formula(paste("cases ~", m_i))
  lm_model <- lm(formula_lm, data = df_scaled_robust_i)
  
  
  # 3. Extract the key numbers
  summ <- summary(gam_model)
  
  # Get smooth term stats (edf, F, p-value)
  # s.table contains the significance of smooth terms
  edf_val <- summ$s.table[1, "edf"]
  p_val   <- summ$s.table[1, "p-value"]
  
  # f_val   <- summ$s.table[1, "F"]

  # Dynamically check whether the model used an F-test or Chi-Square test
  # For families with an estimated dispersion parameter (like Gaussian), it uses an F-test and names the column "F".
  # For families with a known dispersion parameter (and certain robust families), it uses a Chi-Square test and names the column "Chi.sq".
  if ("F" %in% colnames(summ$s.table)) {
    stat_val  <- summ$s.table[1, "F"]
    stat_type <- "F-statistic"
  } else if ("Chi.sq" %in% colnames(summ$s.table)) {
    stat_val  <- summ$s.table[1, "Chi.sq"]
    stat_type <- "Chi-square"
  } else {
    stat_val  <- NA
    stat_type <- "Unknown"
  }
  
  # Get AICs
  aic_gam <- AIC(gam_model)
  aic_lm  <- AIC(lm_model)
  
  # 4. Store in a neat dataframe row
  stats_list[[m]] <- data.frame(
    Metric = m,
    EDF = round(edf_val, 2),                # Effective Degrees of Freedom (>1 means curvy)
    Test_Statistic = round(stat_val, 2),    # Strength of association
    P_Value = p_val,                        # Significance
    AIC_GAM = round(aic_gam, 1),
    AIC_Linear = round(aic_lm, 1),
    Delta_AIC = round(aic_lm - aic_gam, 1), # Positive = GAM is better
    Adj_R_Sq = round(summ$r.sq, 3)    # How much variance explained?
  )

  #####################################
  ## Generate data for viz 
  #####################################
  
  # Generate predictions for the curve 
  #' 1.1 Extrapolation from -2 SD to +2 SD
  # We create a new sequence of data points to draw a smooth line
  # pred_data <- data.frame(
  #   Var_Value = seq(-2.5, 2.5, length.out = 100) # Range of Z-scores
  # )
  
  # A. Define Range based on ACTUAL data (No Extrapolation)
  #' 1.2 Predict only where data exists
  actual_min <- min(df_scaled_robust_i[[m_i]], na.rm = TRUE)
  actual_max <- max(df_scaled_robust_i[[m_i]], na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Create sequence only within real data range
  pred_data <- data.frame(
    Var_Value = seq(actual_min, actual_max, length.out = 100)
  )


  # Rename column to match the current metric name so predict() works
  colnames(pred_data) <- m_i
  
  
  # B. Predict "Terms" (The Critical Fix)
  # type = "terms" returns the Centered Effect (0 = Mean). 
  # This makes "Predicted Change" accurate and aligns with y=0 line.
  # preds <- predict(gam_model , newdata = pred_data, type = "terms", se.fit = TRUE)
  
  # Plot the centred smooth term so zero means the model's average effect.
  # This matches the Figure 6 y-axis and must not be described as a predicted
  # number of deaths.
  preds <- predict(
    gam_model, newdata = pred_data, type = "terms", se.fit = TRUE
  )
  
  # Store clean dataframe
  plot_data_list[[m]] <- data.frame(
    Metric = m,
    x = pred_data[,1], # The Z-score
    y = drop(preds$fit),
    se = drop(preds$se.fit)
  )
}

# Combine `plot data` all into one dataframe
df_cont_curve <- do.call(rbind, plot_data_list)


# Combine `model stats` into one final table
model_stats_table <- do.call(rbind, stats_list) %>%
  # Add a "Significance" column for easier reading
  mutate(Signif_Code = case_when(
    P_Value < 0.001 ~ "***",
    P_Value < 0.01  ~ "**",
    P_Value < 0.05  ~ "*",
    TRUE            ~ "ns"
  )) %>%
  # Sort by strongest non-linearity (optional)
  arrange(desc(Delta_AIC))

                          gsub('_',' ', str_to_lower(outcome_ind)), ' ', cases_meaning_lab, ' (', lc_snr, ")")
```


Effective degrees of freedom (EDF) describe the fitted smooth's complexity:
EDF close to 1 is approximately linear, whereas larger values indicate greater
curvature. Shape descriptions should still be based on the plotted curve and
its uncertainty, not an EDF threshold alone.
 
`F-statistic` (or Chi-sq): The test statistic for the smooth term.
`AIC difference`: A positive linear-minus-GAM value favours the smooth model
among the compared models; it is comparative evidence, not proof of a specific
biological or social response shape.

```{r - gam - parameters, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}

hist(df_scaled_robust_i$cases, nclass = 1000)
min(df_scaled_robust_i$cases, na.rm = T) > 0

# 2. Define competing models
# Model A: The Baseline (Gaussian, no shrinkage)
mod_gaussian <- gam(cases ~ s(x_raw, k=k_i, bs="tp"), 
                    data=df_scaled_robust_i, family=gaussian(), method="REML")

# Model B: The Gold Standard for Skewed Rates (Tweedie, shrinkage)
mod_tweedie <- gam(cases ~ s(x_raw, k=k_i, bs="ts"), 
                   data=df_scaled_robust_i, 
                   # family=tw(), 
                   family = scat(), 
                   method="REML", select=TRUE)

# Model C: The Gamma Alternative (Gamma, shrinkage - only works if cases > 0 strictly)
mod_gamma <- gam(cases ~ s(x_raw, k=k_i, bs="ts"), 
                 data=df_scaled_robust_i, family=Gamma(link="log"), method="REML", select=TRUE)

# 3. Compare Goodness of Fit (AIC)
# Lower AIC is better. A difference of > 2 means the lower model is significantly better.
AIC(mod_gaussian, mod_tweedie, mod_gamma)

# 4. Check the 'k' parameter of your winning model
# Look at the console output: 
# If the p-value for the 'k-index' is > 0.05, your 'k' is perfect.
gam.check(mod_tweedie)
```

```{r - gam plot + density: fig.6, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Define a scaling factor to make the density fit nicely at the bottom
# 0.04 is the height (adjust to make taller/shorter)
# -0.03 is the y-position floor (adjust to move up/down)
density_scale <- 0.01
y_floor <- 0 

# Define where you want the arrows vertically
arrow_y <- 0  # Adjust this value to move arrows up/down
arrow_len <- 0.1 # Length of the arrow tip


#' --- alternatively, use `geom_ribbon`
total_y_range <- max(df_cont_curve$y, na.rm=T) - min(df_cont_curve$y, na.rm=T)
density_height <- 0.15 * total_y_range  # Density will take up 15% of the curve's height
# Set the floor just below the lowest Confidence Interval
# We subtract a tiny buffer (5% of range) so it doesn't touch the CI
y_floor <- min(df_cont_curve$y - 1.96 * df_cont_curve$se, na.rm = TRUE) - (0.05 * total_y_range)
y_floor <- - density_height * 1.1


ggplot() +
  # # --- LAYER 1: The Density Distribution (Replaces Rug) ---
  # geom_density(data = df_cont_raw, 
  #              aes(x = x_raw,

  #              
  #              fill = "gray50", color = NA, alpha = 0.5) +
  
  # --- LAYER 1: The "Floating" Density ---
  # We use geom_ribbon with stat="density".
  # This allows us to hard-code 'ymin' to our floor, preventing the "fill to zero" issue.
  geom_ribbon(data = df_cont_raw, 
              aes(x = x_raw, 
                  ymin = y_floor,

              stat = "density",

              linewidth = 0.1,       # Thin outline
              alpha = 0.6) +
```

```{r - gam plot + density-ggExtra [x], eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
library(ggExtra)  # For ggMarginal
library(cowplot)  # For combining the individual plots

# List to store the final plots
final_plots_list <- list()

for (m in metrics) {
  
  # 1. Filter data for just THIS metric
  # We need the RAW data for the marginal density (so it's accurate)
  # and the CURVE data for the line.
  data_subset <- df_cont_raw %>% filter(Metric == m)
  curve_subset <- df_cont_curve %>% filter(Metric == m)
  
  # 2. Create the Base Plot
  # Note: We keep the theme very minimal to save space in the grid
  p <- ggplot() +
    # Dummy point layer (invisible) so ggMarginal knows where the data is
    geom_point(data = data_subset, aes(x = x_raw, y = 0), alpha = 0) +
    
    # Confidence Interval
    geom_ribbon(data = curve_subset, aes(x = x, ymin = y - 1.96 * se, ymax = y + 1.96 * se), 
                fill = "#2c7bb6", alpha = 0.2) +
    
    # Main Curve
    geom_line(data = curve_subset, aes(x = x, y = y), 
              color = "#2c7bb6", linewidth = 1) +
    
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.01, 0.17)) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-4, 7)) +
    
    # Reference Lines
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "gray50") +
    
    # Labels (We keep titles strictly for the Metric name)
    labs(title = m, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 8, face = "bold"), # Center title
      axis.text = element_text(size = 8)
    )

  # 3. Apply ggMarginal
  # type = "density": Smooth curve
  # margins = "x": Only show density on the bottom (x-axis)
  # size = 4: Ratio of main plot to marginal plot height
  p_marginal <- ggMarginal(p, type = "density", margins = "x", 
                           fill = "gray80", color = NA, size = 10)
  
  # 4. Save to list
  final_plots_list[[m]] <- p_marginal
}

# 5. Combine into one grid
# adjust 'ncol' depending on how many metrics you have (e.g., 2 or 3)
combined_plot <- plot_grid(plotlist = final_plots_list, ncol = 3)

final_figure <- ggdraw(add_sub(combined_plot, "Vulnerability Metric (Standardized Z-Score)", 
                               vpadding = grid::unit(0, "lines"), y = 6, x = 0.5, vjust = 4.5))
```

```{r - gam + box [x], eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# 1. Prepare Data: Pivot Long and Ensure Quintiles are calculated
plot_data_hybrid <- df_scaled_robust %>%
  select(cases, all_of(metrics)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(metrics), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Z_Score") %>%
  group_by(Metric) %>%
  mutate(
    # Recalculate Quintiles (just to be safe)
    Quintile = ntile(Z_Score, 5),
    Quintile_Factor = factor(Quintile)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# 2. Calculate the 'Position' for each Boxplot
# We want the boxplot to sit at the MEDIAN Z-score of that quintile
boxplot_positions <- plot_data_hybrid %>%
  group_by(Metric, Quintile_Factor) %>%
  summarise(
    center_x = median(Z_Score, na.rm = TRUE), # Where to put the box on X-axis
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 3. Create the Plot
ggplot() +
  # --- LAYER 1: The Raw Data (Optional, faint jitter to show density) ---
  geom_point(data = plot_data_hybrid, aes(x = Z_Score, y = cases, color = Quintile_Factor), 
             alpha = 0.05, size = 0.5) +
  
  # --- LAYER 2: The Boxplots (Positioned correctly on X-axis) ---
  # We use 'group' to force distinct boxes, but map 'x' to the continuous value
  geom_boxplot(data = plot_data_hybrid, 
               aes(x = Z_Score, y = cases, group = Quintile_Factor, fill = Quintile_Factor), 
               outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.3, width = 0.5) +
  
  # --- LAYER 3: The GAM Curve (The Trend) ---
  # We use geom_smooth directly here
  geom_smooth(data = plot_data_hybrid, aes(x = Z_Score, y = cases), 
              method = "gam", color = "purple", linewidth = 1, se = FALSE) +
  
  # --- Styling ---
  # facet_wrap(~Metric, scales = "fixed") + # Fixed scales to compare magnitude
  facet_wrap(~Metric, scale = 'free') +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Spectral") +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Spectral") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.15)) +
  
  labs(title = "Synthesis: Continuous Trends vs. Grouped Quintiles",
       subtitle = "Black Line = GAM Mean Trend | Boxes = Quintile Distribution (Median/IQR)",
       x = "Vulnerability Metric (Standardized Z-Score)",
       y = "Predicted Change in Cases") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

*glm*

Summary of Recommendations
- lm (Linear)	                    Data is normally distributed (Rare for cases).	
- glm.nb (Negative Binomial)	    Data is counts, skewed, variance > mean. (Most likely)	IRR (Rate Ratio)
- lme4::glmer.nb (Mixed Effects)	You have data from many different cities/regions and need to control for that grouping.	IRR (Rate Ratio)

*glm.nb (Negative Binomial), poisson, and Gamma cannot handle negative numbers. They will crash or give wrong answers.*

```{r - glm_nb [x], eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}

library(broom)
library(purrr)
library(MASS) # Required for glm.nb

# 1. Standardize your metrics (Z-scores)
# This ensures the Rate Ratio is "per 1 SD increase" in deprivation
# df_scaled_robust

# 2. Run Negative Binomial Regression for each metric
models_nb <- map_dfr(metrics, function(m) {
  
  # Formula: cases ~ metric + offset(log(population))
  # Note: If you have a 'population' column, use offset() to model RATES, not just counts.
  # If 'cases' is already a rate, remove the offset.
  
  formula_str <- paste("cases ~", m) # Add "+ offset(log(population))" if 'cases' is a raw count
  
  tryCatch({
    model <- glm.nb(as.formula(formula_str), data = df_scaled_robust)
    
    # Tidy the results, asking for Exponentiated coefficients (Rate Ratios)
    broom::tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) %>%
      filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
      mutate(Metric = m)
  }, error = function(e) return(NULL)) # Skips if model fails to converge
}) %>%
  mutate(
    Significance = ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "Significant", "NS"),
    Stars = case_when(
      p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE            ~ ""
    )
  )

# 3. Plot the Rate Ratios (Forest Plot)
ggplot(models_nb, aes(x = estimate, y = reorder(Metric, estimate), color = Significance)) +
  # Reference line is now at 1 (Rate Ratio of 1 = No Effect), not 0
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), height = 0.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Stars), vjust = -0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Significant" = "#2c7bb6", "NS" = "gray70")) +
  
  labs(title = "Impact of Vulnerability on Disease Risk (Negative Binomial)",
       subtitle = "Values represent Incidence Rate Ratios (IRR) per 1 SD increase in metric",
       x = "Incidence Rate Ratio (IRR) [1 = No Change]",
       y = "") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.8, 0.1))

f <- paste0('./figures/', 'health_outcome_equity_esIRR_', lc_snr, '.png')
# ggsave(plot = last_plot(), filename = f, width = 7, height = 5, units = 'in', dpi = 300)
```

```{r - one, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
data_bivariate <- df_cont %>%
  mutate(x_var = .data[[sv_i]], 
         y_var = cases) %>%
  bi_class(x = x_var, y = y_var, style = "quantile", dim = 3)

pal_i <- 'DkBlue'
pal_i <- 'DkCyan'

# 2. Create the Map
map <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = data_bivariate, aes(fill = bi_class), color = 'gray', size = 0.05, show.legend = FALSE) +
  bi_scale_fill(pal = pal_i, dim = 3) + # Palette options: "DkBlue", "DkCyan", "GrPink", etc.
  # labs(title = "Income Deprivation vs. Preventable Cases") +
  bi_theme(base_size = 10) +
  # This removes the white box behind the square legend
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA)
  )

# 3. Create the Square Legend
legend <- bi_legend(pal = pal_i,
                    dim = 3,
                    xlab = "Deprivation ",
                    ylab = outcome_lab,
                    size = 8) +
  theme(
    # This sets the overall background of the legend plot to transparent
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    # This ensures no other rectangle elements (like borders) have color
    rect = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA)
  )


# 4. Combine Map and Legend
final_plot <- ggdraw() +
  draw_plot(map, 0, 0, 1, 1) +
  draw_plot(legend, x = 0.7, y = 0.05, width = 0.2, height = 0.2) # Adjust x/y position of legend

print(final_plot)
```

```{r - loop - fig.7, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}

# List of your metrics
# metrics <- c("pIncomeDeprivation", "pBAME", "pSocial_housing", "p75over")
names(df_cont)


font_size <- 6

# Create empty list to store plots
plot_list <- list()


# Loop through each metric
for (var in metrics) {
  
  # Get label with fallback
  var_label <- if (var %in% names(label_map)) label_map[var] else var
  
  # 1. Prepare data (Note: We rename columns dynamically for bi_class to work easier)
  temp_gdf <- df_cont %>%
    mutate(x_var = .data[[var]], 
           y_var = cases * health_outcome_direction) %>%
    bi_class(x = x_var, y = y_var, style = "quantile", dim = 3)
  
  
  # 1.2 count each bivariate and save as csv
  temp_gdf_stat <- temp_gdf %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(svi_var = var,
                  outcome_ind = outcome_ind,
                  lc_snr = lc_snr,
                  bi_class = as.character(bi_class),
                  bi_class = gsub('-', '_', bi_class)) %>%
    group_by(outcome_ind, svi_var, lc_snr, bi_class) %>%
    count()
  
  fname_csv = paste0('./figures/equity_map_biscale/', 
                    paste('equity_map_health_stat_bivar', outcome_ind, var, lc_snr, sep = '_'),
                    '.csv')
  readr::write_csv(x = temp_gdf_stat, file = fname_csv)

  
  # 2. Map
  map <- ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = temp_gdf, aes(fill = bi_class), color = NA, size = 0.05, show.legend = FALSE) +
    bi_scale_fill(pal = pal_i, dim = 3) +
    # labs(title = paste0(var_label, " vs. Cases")) +
    bi_theme(base_size = font_size) +
    theme(
      plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
      panel.spacing = unit(0, "pt"),
      legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
      legend.box.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_blank(), 
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA)
    )
    
  
  # 3. Legend
  legend <- bi_legend(pal = pal_i, dim = 3, xlab = "Vulnerability", ylab = outcome_lab, size = font_size) +
    theme(
      # This sets the overall background of the legend plot to transparent
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
      plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
      panel.spacing = unit(0, "pt"),
      # This ensures no other rectangle elements (like borders) have color
      rect = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA)
  )
  
  # 4. Combine
  final_plot <- 
    # ggdraw() +
    ggdraw(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    theme(
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
      plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
  ) + 
    draw_plot(map, 0, 0, 1, 1) +
    draw_plot(legend, x = 0.7, y = 0.06, width = 0.3, height = 0.3) +
    draw_label(var_label, x = 0.86, y = 0.05, fontface = 'bold', size = font_size+1) 
  
  # Store in list
  plot_list[[var]] <- final_plot
  
  # # 5. Save
  # f <- paste0('./figures/equity_map_biscale/', 
  #             paste('equity_map_health', outcome_ind, var, lc_snr, ymd, outcome_d, sep = '_'), '.png'); f
  # ggsave(filename = f, plot = final_plot, bg = "transparent", dpi = 600, width = 7/2, height = 4.8/2, units = 'in', device = ragg::agg_png)
}



# Combine all plots ------------------------------------------------------------
combined_plot <- plot_grid(
  plotlist = plot_list,
  ncol = 2,           # 2 columns
  nrow = 2,           # 2 rows (adjust based on number of metrics)
  labels = 'auto',
  label_size = 11,
  align = 'hv'        # align horizontally and vertically
)

# Save combined plot
ggsave(
  filename = paste0('./figures/equity_map_biscale/', 
                    paste('equity_map_health', outcome_ind, 'combined', lc_snr, ymd, outcome_d, sep = '_'),
                    '.png'),

  bg = "transparent",

  width = 7,         # Wider for 2 columns
  height = 4.8,        # Taller for 2 rows
  device = ragg::agg_png
)
```

### Legacy Fig. 7c summary (retained for audit only)

The class-count plots below used scenario-specific quantiles and incomplete
stacks, so they are excluded from the manuscript figure.

```{r - stat - change - load data, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}

## plot selected lc scenarios
lc_snr_i <- c('Green30', 'Target30')


## load in all the relevant csv

stat_bi <- list.files(
  path = "./figures/equity_map_biscale/",
  pattern = "^equity_map_health_stat_bivar.*\\.csv$",
  full.names = TRUE
) %>%
  purrr::map_dfr(
    ~ read_csv(.x, show_col_types = F) %>%
      mutate(file = basename(.x))
  )


# save data
saveRDS(object = stat_bi, file = "./figures/equity_map_biscale/stat_bi.rds")


stat_bi_viz <- stat_bi %>%
  select(-file) %>%
  group_by(outcome_ind, svi_var, lc_snr) %>%
  mutate(
    total_tracts = sum(n),
    pct = round(n / total_tracts * 100, 1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%

  filter(bi_class %in% c('3_1', '1_3', '2_3', '3_3')) %>%
  filter(lc_snr %in% lc_snr_i) %>%
  arrange(outcome_ind, svi_var, bi_class, lc_snr) %>%
  as.data.frame()
```

### Figure 7: paired Green30-Target30 equity comparison

The production workflow is maintained in
`code/equity-health-fig7-production.Rmd`. It pairs identical LSOAs, applies
Green30 mortality-benefit tertiles to both scenarios, adds paired-bootstrap
sensitivity intervals, and records the 2021 population/mortality assumption.
When `data/derived/lsoa_population_2021.csv` is available, the distributional
benefit is expressed per 100,000 residents.

```{r fig-7-production, echo=FALSE, out.width='100%'}
fig7_ab_path <- "./figures/equity_map_biscale_revised_equal_area/fig7_ab_upgraded.png"
fig7_cd_path <- "./figures/equity_map_biscale_revised_equal_area/fig7_cd_upgraded.png"

if (!all(file.exists(c(fig7_ab_path, fig7_cd_path)))) {
  stop(
    "Run code/equity-health-fig7-production.Rmd before rendering Figure 7."
  )
}

knitr::include_graphics(fig7_ab_path)
knitr::include_graphics(fig7_cd_path)
```
